title: Your stomach growl isn't really your stomach

lines: That stomach growl? It's mostly coming from somewhere else.
The noise is gas and fluid being squeezed through your small intestine by waves of muscle called peristalsis.

beats.label: between cleaning waves
lines: And between meals, a cleaning wave sweeps through your gut every ninety to two hundred thirty minutes.

beats.title: What it sweeps
lines: It pushes leftover food and bacteria down toward the large intestine.
That sweep is behind the rumbling you hear when you're hungry.

beats.label: growl
lines: And an empty stomach makes it louder, because the empty space amplifies the sound of moving air.
In one study, a four hundred fifty calorie breakfast paused it for about two hundred thirteen minutes.
So next time your belly growls, it's not complaining. It's your gut's housekeeper, tidying up between meals.

sources.claim: Rumbling is gas and fluid moving through the small intestine, propelled by peristalsis; heard near but not actually within the stomach.
Louder rumbles when hungry; the sound of air in the stomach is amplified by the empty space.

The migrating motor complex occurs every 90-230 minutes between meals, causes the hunger rumbling, sweeps indigestible material and bacteria toward the large intestine, and acts as an 'interdigestive housekeeper'.
Eating interrupts the MMC; one study found a 450 kcal breakfast made it disappear for 213 +/- 48 minutes.
